chapter: Style and old New Orleans customs
title: Having his own bass style that others cannot copy
summary: Players try to copy his bass playing and fail; he insists every musician needs a style of his own.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Your style just comes to you. That's right.

That's right. I make whatever comes in my mind to make it and ain't nobody else going to ever be a player. See, because when I find out they're playing the way they think they got it, I'll play it and put something else in.
Yeah, well I never have heard anybody else ever do that. They ain't going to never do it. No, I mean I've heard them try to copy and all that. That's right. They can't cut.

They tried to copy. I don't know. I went down to Jaffer's couple times and he asked me to play it. I play it and he get his horn and play along with me and I just take down. I say good lick. It's all right. She makes the hoop. They don't make it. Brown tried to make it. Minor tried to make it. I don't worry about them. I make it. Make it when I get ready and put anything in it I want. It's like Larry come there one night. Larry said, I never heard a man make a triple turn on the best way to do. And he brought some white boy there with him and the white boy said, I never could triple turn. Larry said, play it again. Make it again. I know I don't be dumb. I know he's trying to catch on. You might make something sound like it. But you can't make what the other man made. You can't do it to see if you're like them boys write copies of Louis Armstrong and style, copies of Al Hoyt style. But when they play it, if they don't have a style of their own, they ain't play nothing right at all. You got to have your own style of music. If everybody played the same way, music wouldn't be worth two cents to listen to it. No. No. No, it wouldn't be any good at all. No, no it wouldn't be any good at all.
